script:
You are a professional screenwriter.

Write a modern screenplay.

Constraints:
- No guns
- No gun violence
- No weapon combat
- No graphic violence
- No copyrighted characters
- Completely original story

Requirements:
- 10–15 scenes
- Proper screenplay format
- INT/EXT scene headers
- Dialogue in uppercase character format
- Realistic pacing

Genre: Family
Theme: forgiveness

Begin screenplay.

FADE IN:

INT. KITCHEN - DAY

Grace, a 35-YEAR-OLD FIRST-TIME MOTHER, stands in her kitchen. She clutches her infant son, JAMES, as tears stream down her face.

GRACE
(whispering)
Why can't I do this? Why can't I be a good mom?

James coos and gurgles, oblivious to his mother's distress.

Suddenly, the front door creaks open. Grace turns around, her heart pounding.

INT. LIVING ROOM - DAY

Grace's EX-HUSBAND, MIKE, enters the house carrying a large bag. He sets it down and approaches his wife.

MIKE
(softly)
Hi, Grace. I brought groceries.

Grace's expression is guarded.

GRACE
(sternly)
What are you doing here, Mike?

MIKE
(sighs)
I just wanted to talk. I know we've had our differences, but I've been thinking a lot lately. I miss James, and I miss you.

Grace looks away, her voice shaking.

GRACE
You left us, Mike. You left me to raise our son alone. How can we just pick up where we left off?

MIKE
(nervously)
I know I made mistakes, Grace. I know I hurt you. But I've been in therapy, and I've been working on myself. I want to make things right.

Grace hesitates, then nods.

GRACE
Fine. We can talk. But we're not getting back together.

INT. KITCHEN - NIGHT

Grace sits at the kitchen table, her eyes red from crying. Mike enters, carrying a tray of sandwiches.

MIKE
(setting down the tray)
I made us lunch.

Grace looks up at her ex-husband, her expression wary.

GRACE
(angrily)
What do you want from me, Mike?

MIKE
(sitting across from her)
I want to be a part of James's life. I want to be a good father. And I want to make amends for the pain I caused you.

GRACE
(sighs)
What can you do, Mike? How can you make it up to me?

MIKE
(thoughtfully)
I can help out around the house. I can take James for weekends. I can be a reliable source of support for you.

Grace thinks for a moment, then nods.

GRACE
Fine. We'll give it a try.

INT. PARK - DAY

Grace, Mike, and James sit on a blanket in the park. They share a picnic, and James plays in the grass.

GRACE
(smiling at her son)
I'm glad you're happy, James.

MIKE
(looking at his son)
He is a wonderful boy, Grace. I'm lucky to have him in my life.

Grace looks at her ex-husband, her expression softening.

GRACE
(quietly)
I'm glad you're happy too, Mike.

INT. LIVING ROOM - NIGHT

Grace and Mike sit on the couch, James fast asleep in his bassinet nearby.

MIKE
(looking at his wife)
I never thought I'd be able to say this, but I'm grateful for you, Grace. You've been an incredible mother to James.

GRACE
(smiling)
And you've been an incredible father. We make a good team.

MIKE
(leans in to kiss her)
I know we've had our struggles, but I believe we can overcome them. I believe in us.

Grace looks into her husband's eyes and nods.

GRACE
I believe in us too.

FADE OUT.

END OF SCREENPLAY.
